root_cause_label: Greedy local heuristics cannot reliably navigate a stochastic maze to gold; repeated solution rewrites all share the same fundamental inadequacy
one_sentence_failure_summary: All solution variants rely on myopic greedy heuristics (prefer higher elevation, pick up blocks) that cannot reliably reach gold in a stochastic maze, causing every trial to spin indefinitely without ever generating test_results.json, while the agent exhausts its budget in a thrash loop of create-copy-timeout cycles.
t_err_evidence: Agent creates solution.js using coordinate-based BFS pathfinding, but game only provides relative cell info without absolute positions.
t_commit_evidence: From step 5 onward, every solution variant the agent writes is a greedy local heuristic; the agent never implements a proper exploration-with-memory algorithm (e.g., proper BFS/DFS with position tracking). The test run at step 6 immediately hangs, confirming the approach is broken, yet all subsequent attempts follow the same pattern.
t_surface_evidence: node test_runner.js hangs with no output after 10 seconds, exit_code=-1.
trigger_explanation: The model's plan is directionally correct (explore maze, collect blocks, build stairs, reach gold) but every concrete implementation it generates is a local greedy heuristic that lacks systematic exploration; with a stochastic 18x18 grid containing walls and random block placement, these heuristics cannot guarantee termination. The model cannot generate a working maze-traversal algorithm with position memory despite multiple attempts.
